verdicts.justification: Repro reproduced exactly: 'A last row: [0.25714286 0.25714286 0.25714286]' / 'B first row: [0.74285714 0.74285714 0.74285714]' -- constant datasets are corrupted at their edges, proving the smoothing kernel runs across the A/B boundary. readme.md lines 80-81 promise 'applies a per-dataset manipulation (Normalize, ZScore, Smooth, ...)'. Silent numerically-wrong results on a plain documented call: critical is fair.

Repro reproduced exactly: 'zA col means: [0.98908681 0.99013639 0.99117994]; zB col means: [-0.98908681 -0.99013639 -0.99117994]' -- stacked statistics, not per-dataset (per-dataset would give ~0 means). readme.md line 80-81 says manip 'applies a per-dataset manipulation (Normalize, ZScore, ...)' and the ZScore docstring says 'z-score each column independently'. Upgraded doc->major: users following the docs get wrong z-scores, not just wrong prose.

All three retired kwargs die identically: "AttributeError : Line2D.set() got an unexpected keyword argument 'group'" (same for 'model' and 'model_params'). The comparison point is real: hyp.plot(x, align=True) raises "ValueError : align=True was removed in hypertools 1.0; specify the algorithm instead, e.g. align='hyper' or align='SRM'." -- so the migration-message machinery exists and just doesn't cover these.

Repro: hyp.cluster(x, cluster='KMeans', n_clusters=2, ndims=3) with no reduce= returned "type: <class 'list'> len: 120" with "warnings: []" -- no error, no warning, ndims silently ignored. readme.md line 139 claims "cluster(ndims=...) arguments were removed", yet hyp.cluster's docstring still documents "ndims : int or None -- Passed through to the reduce stage (as ndims=) when reduce=". README wording contradicts reality.

readme.md line 52 documents 'hypertools.plot.colors.mat2colors'. Attribute access gives "AttributeError : 'function' object has no attribute 'colors'" (hypertools.plot is <class 'function'>), and a fresh-interpreter 'import hypertools.plot.colors as pc' gives "ImportError: cannot import name 'colors' from 'plot' (unknown location)". The documented path is unreachable exactly as claimed.

With max_dims=14 on 6-column data: len(res['average']) == 12 (components 2..13, exclusive endpoint) and values go flat at 1.0 from component ~6 onward: [0.9925 0.9981 0.9991 0.9998 1. 1. 1. 1. 1. 1. 1. 1.]; only warning emitted was the generic 'When input data is large...'. hyp.reduce(x6, ndims=10) silently returned shape (100, 6). describe docstring says only 'Maximum number of dimensions to consider' (reads inclusive). Evidence B5 PNG independently shows the x-axis ending at 13.

Repro reproduced exactly: "ValueError: RGBA sequence should have length 3 or 4" raised from matplotlib/colors.py (traceback through _to_rgba_no_colorcycle). readme.md lines 56-59 advertise 'a dict form for per-dataset alpha/color/lighting/smoothing control', which reads as an invitation to pass per-dataset lists as dict values -- the exact form that crashes with no hypertools-level message.

Verified: pyproject dependencies include 'dill>=0.3.8', 'pykalman>=0.11', 'statsmodels>=0.14', 'pydata-wrangler>=0.5.1'; the readme.md Requirements list (lines 172-183) omits all four. Mitigating note: line 185 does say 'All Python dependencies are declared in pyproject.toml and installed automatically by pip', so the deferral exists -- but the itemized list still presents itself as the dependency list and omits pydata-wrangler, the data-wrangling core. Doc severity fair.
Verified verbatim at readme.md ~line 221: the block opens '@ARTICLE {,' -- empty citation key. An entry with no key cannot be \cite'd, so the provided BibTeX is unusable as shipped.

Verified from readme.md lines 252-306: the five python blocks reference list_of_arrays/list_of_labels (Plot, Align, Describe), array (Cluster), and blob_a/blob_b (Surfaces) -- none is defined and no note marks them as placeholders, so each fails with NameError if pasted. Common README idiom, hence style is the right severity.

Repro re-run: colorbar axis y-tick labels are exactly ['1', '2', '3'] despite hue=['A']*50+['B']*50+['C']*50 (verified programmatically from the returned Figure, and visually in evidence C5_colorbar_discrete.png which shows segments labeled 1/2/3). User-supplied category names are dropped.

Evidence C3_multicolor_line_continuous_hue.png inspected: the colorbar is red/salmon at value 0 and returns to red/salmon at the top (~175-190) -- the cyclic hls palette wraps, making a continuous scale's endpoints indistinguishable. Claim is fair as a design nit.

Repro reproduced the warning verbatim: 'Cannot reduce the dimensionality of a single row of data. Return zeros length of ndims' -- garbled grammar as claimed. Note the title's 'silently' is slightly overstated (a UserWarning does fire), but the substantive claim (zeros plotted, garbled message) is accurate.

Independently re-timed with six fresh 5-9 word sentences: 'elapsed: 109.8 s' for hyp.plot(texts, vectorizer='Word2Vec', semantic=None, reduce='PCA') -- matching the auditor's 110.1 s. readme.md lines 92-98 give exactly this recipe with no cost caveat; plot()'s corpus docstring notes the pretrained shortcut only applies to default models, so the non-default Word2Vec vectorizer trains on the full 'wiki' corpus silently.
